title: Knowledge check: Form Usability and Accessibility

questions.prompt: Which source-syllabus topic is explicitly covered by “Form Usability and Accessibility”?
options: Flask's purpose in Python web development
questions.explanation: The PDF lists “Labels and associated input fields” under lesson 65, “Form Usability and Accessibility”. Keep this subtopic aligned to its module and confirm version-sensitive details in the official Flask documentation.

questions.prompt: When applying “Form Usability and Accessibility” in a real Flask application, which approach is the most reliable?
options: Trust the browser and skip server-side checks.
Change several parts at once and infer success from one happy-path request.
Use a small reproducible example and test both expected behavior and a meaningful failure boundary.
Expose internal tracebacks to the caller to simplify debugging.
questions.answer_key: Use a small reproducible example and test both expected behavior and a meaningful failure boundary.
questions.explanation: For form usability and accessibility, use the matching official documentation, a narrow example, and a test of both normal and invalid conditions. Browser validation alone and exposed tracebacks are not reliable safeguards.

questions.prompt: Which design principle best complements “Form Usability and Accessibility” as the course moves toward production?
options: Assume a green diagram proves correctness without running a test.
Assume Flask automatically provides a database, authentication system and task queue.
Treat a development server or debug mode as the production deployment plan.
Separate Flask core behavior from optional extension or infrastructure behavior, validate untrusted input at the server boundary, and document the runtime assumptions.
questions.answer_key: Separate Flask core behavior from optional extension or infrastructure behavior, validate untrusted input at the server boundary, and document the runtime assumptions.
questions.explanation: Flask is a lightweight framework whose databases, account management, caching and task queues commonly come from separately selected tools. Verify trust boundaries and runtime assumptions with tests.

notes: Answer keys and explanations are kept in repository-side question files. Public endpoints should expose choices, not answer_key fields, until server-side grading returns per-answer feedback.
